name: Skwala Stonefly Adult
imitates: The olive-and-yellow adult skwala stonefly of late winter and early spring, with a short tail, dark moose wing and a small parachute post; fish it along the banks in the first warm spells.
recipe: Pale yellow dubbing, a little olive mixed in
Calf body hair or white synthetic

steps.text: Smash the barb, coat the shank with a thin layer of Flexament, and cover it with thread. Just above the barb tie on a small unstacked clump of moose body hair as a short tail.

At the same spot dub a small black egg-sac ball and tie in black V-Rib. Dub a medium pale yellow body with a little olive mixed in, ending about a third of a shank behind the eye. Color the top with an olive marker.

Stretch the V-Rib thin and rib the body in even turns. At the front of the body tie in about eight strands of black Crystal Flash and a clean clump of moose body hair, reaching to the end of the tail.

Tie a small clump of calf hair or white synthetic at the wing base and trim it to about 3/8 inch as the post. Fold a strand of stretch floss over the post and tie it down so the two ends form an X of legs, with a tiny drop of glue at the post base.
Tie in a saddle hackle at the post base, dub over the tie-in, and wind it up and back down the post. Tie off behind the eye, form a small head and whip finish. The finished fly.

source.name: Spring Creek Flycraft and Guide Service (GB Flycasters pattern page)
